s1-foundation.summaryMarkdown: All three findings are repaired and verified in source and tests. Non-root Root steps now authenticate with an interactive `sudo -v` first; a refused prompt returns Declined without running the command, a failing wrapped command stays an ordinary failure, and the fake-sudo tests prove the argv, env, cwd, decline and Print-never-calls-sudo paths (Unix-only, run under WSL by the coordinator and compiled out on Windows). The WM_SETTINGCHANGE broadcast is best-effort with a failing-broadcast test. quote_windows follows CommandLineToArgvW rules and is covered by a rendering test. REPO-1, REPO-3, HOST-1, HOST-2, HOST-3 are proven by their own groups; REPO-2's workflow matches the criterion and its first green run awaits the first push.

s1b-toolchain-pins.summaryMarkdown: All three findings repaired and verified: the nightly setup step now exists in both pr-test.yml jobs that run the xtask WASM build; the reference's closing grep is the sprint pattern and finds nothing in RayX or in Gpux (vendor and crates excluded, reason stated); the stale doc comment is fixed. PINX-1..3 hold; forbidden paths untouched. Excluding Gpux crates from the nightly grep is reasonable: its only two matches are a cargo feature and an example toolchain file, not pins.

s2-pins-and-base-setup.summaryMarkdown: All seven findings are repaired in source and covered by new tests in each task's own group. Discovery no longer lets rustup install anything and still resolves project pins from manifests when cargo or the pinned toolchain is missing; the Windows toolchain probe is native-triple aware; dpkg, marker lifecycle, PowerShell quoting and Homebrew sudo gaps are closed. PIN-1..2 and SETUP-1..4 pass against current source and tests.

s3-optional-sets-and-doctor.summaryMarkdown: All ten findings are repaired and verified in source and tests. Node, corepack and pnpm are found on PATH (without WSL /mnt entries) and in the install locations, and run by absolute path. `with_node_path` puts the found Node directory and the user bin directory at the front of PATH for the pnpm probe and every node_command, so the corepack shim finds `node` right after an install. Xcode versions come from version.plist, the pin drives selection, the AVD probe filters log lines, the system image follows the platform pin, the batch tools start by full path, doctor records versions and reports usable hardware adapters, and the Playwright and GPU probes are idempotent. Accepted as disclosed: the Windows Update fallback for NVIDIA, AMD and Qualcomm, and no DXGI driver date.

s4-app-pipeline.summaryMarkdown: All ten criteria are implemented and backed by real source and test anchors; the 18 sprint checks passed at this snapshot, and `cargo test --lib app::` re-run here gives 103 passed. Grammar, project-agnostic resolution (workspace root from `cargo metadata`, entry-crate dependency copied from the app's own `rayx` source, `[patch]` from the selected root, `gpux-fonts` via metadata, pinned nightly and locked wasm-bindgen, host triples, no re-exec), the Playwright package resolution and embedded template, `test host`, `fmt` and the PINX-2 JDK 21 pins all check out, and no app name or RayX path is special outside help text. The one minor defect found (unsupported test/deploy targets ran the prerequisite step first, finding `s4-f1-unsupported-targets-install-first`) is repaired by `check_supported` and covered by a new test in `tests/app_prereqs.rs`. Observations, not findings: the Gpux `.agentx/tasks/gpux-cross-platform-test-lanes/*` records still say "JDK 17" (historical runtime records; every source, workflow and doc file says 21); `playwright.rs` duplicates the absolute-path pnpm lookup of `setup/test_tools.rs`; the moved app pipeline's `std::process::Command` use is the recorded exception.

s5-wsl-release-update.summaryMarkdown: Passed at the repaired snapshot. WSL-1/2/3 and REL-1/2 hold as in the first pass (plan, clone, status, dist config and installer receipt, axoupdater flow). The three WSL-4 findings are repaired in f866887 and verified: the vhdx path now reaches the elevated script as base64 data (a path with U+2019 round-trips through PowerShell, no code position holds it), compact refuses a non-.vhdx, control-character or missing disk before fstrim and `wsl --shutdown`, the script ends in `exit $code` taken from `$LASTEXITCODE` of the attach script (detach cannot overwrite it), and `rm -rf` runs only on paths whose last component is target, artifacts or artifacts-temp with no quote or control character (`linux_dir` also rejects control characters). `cargo test --test wsl_disk --test wsl_plan` passes (21 and 18 tests). WSL-4's real compaction, WSL-1's end-to-end run and REL-1/REL-2's first release and download stay manual. Residual risks for the first tag: no cross build runs before it (`pr-run-mode = plan`), and `aws-lc-sys` (via axoupdater, reqwest, rustls) cross-builds for aarch64-pc-windows-msvc through cargo-xwin; cut it as a prerelease. Nits left: a 3-character `\?\` trim in `run()` of src/setup/wsl.rs never matches (harmless), `setup --wsl --check` without the distribution reports the missing-user error, and a reboot needed after `wsl --install` is reported as the missing-user case.

s6-rayx-migration.summaryMarkdown: MIG-1 and MIG-2 hold at snapshot 544a2f5a. MIG-1: xtask keeps only the three chores and its 30 tests pass. MIG-2: CI installs `rayx` at a pinned CLI revision and calls `rayx setup --test --yes` and `rayx app`; the docs, READMEs, agent files, skill and the two tools-node scripts use `rayx`; the removed-command grep is empty and `mdbook build docs` succeeds. The four prose findings (s6-f1 to s6-f4) are repaired, and the from-source install command now names the pushed branch that holds the package.

findings.descriptionMarkdown:
**Expected (HOST-2):** a `Root` step on Linux/macOS runs through `sudo` when not root, and declining the `sudo` prompt stops the step with a clear message, not a crash; the check description requires this to be proven by `tests/command_runner.rs`.

**Observed:** `src/host/runner.rs:374-382` maps a declined `sudo` to `RunError::Declined` only when the sudo process has no exit code (killed by a signal). Real declines do not take that path: a failed or empty password, Ctrl+D or `sudo: a password is required` all make `sudo` exit with code 1, which is returned as an ordinary `Outcome` (and `run_checked` reports `` `sudo ...` exited with code 1`` with no mention of a declined prompt for interactive specs). Ctrl+C sends SIGINT to the whole foreground process group, so `rayx` itself dies before it can map anything. The Declined branch is therefore effectively unreachable. In addition, `sudo_wrapped` (`runner.rs:439-455`: `env K=V` forwarding, cwd, inherited stdin) and the `Privilege::Root` execute branch have no test at all: `tests/command_runner.rs` covers sudo only as a printed string (Print mode) and the already-root direct path, and the declined case only through the scripted `Elevator` (the Windows/UAC half). The `sudo` half of the last HOST-2 bullet is thus neither correctly implemented nor proven.

**Repair:** (1) Before running a `Root` step as non-root, authenticate with an interactive, console-inheriting `sudo -v` (still no password handling by `rayx`); a non-zero exit from `sudo -v` is a refused/declined prompt and returns `RunError::Declined` with the existing clear message, while a non-zero exit of the wrapped command stays a normal failure. Keep the signal case as Declined too. (2) Add `#[cfg(unix)]` tests in `tests/command_runner.rs` that put a fake `sudo` shell script in a temporary directory on `PATH` (or unit-test `sudo_wrapped`) to prove the argv (`sudo env K=V program args`), cwd propagation, that a failing fake `sudo -v` yields `Declined` with the 'did not run' message and does not run the command, and that an approving one runs the command. Print mode must stay side-effect free.

**Expected:** the persisted PATH edit is the outcome; `WM_SETTINGCHANGE` is a best-effort notification, and `rayx` tells the user to open a new shell.

**Observed:** `prepend_to_windows_path` (`src/host/path_env.rs:190-191`) returns `Err` when `broadcast_change` fails, and `RegistryPathStore::broadcast_change` (`path_env.rs:494-496`) returns an error whenever `SendMessageTimeoutW` returns 0, which also happens on a timeout caused by one slow top-level window (with `GetLastError` possibly 0). The registry value has then already been written, so the caller reports a failed step for a change that took effect, and a retry says `AlreadyPresent` without broadcasting.

**Repair:** make the broadcast non-fatal (ignore or return it separately, for example as a warning field on the result), keeping the `Added` result and the new-shell notice; add a `MemoryPathStore` test with a failing broadcast showing `Added` is still returned.

**Expected:** the command line `WindowsElevator` builds runs the argument it was given.

**Observed:** `quote_windows` (`src/host/runner.rs:565-575`) wraps an argument containing spaces in quotes without doubling backslashes that precede the closing quote, so a directory argument such as `C:\Program Files\Tool\` becomes `"C:\Program Files\Tool\"`, which the target program's command-line parser reads as an escaped quote. The elevator already rejects `"`, `%` and line breaks for this class of problem but not this one; `render` (Print) has the same text, so `--check` would show a line that does not match what really runs.

**Repair:** double the run of backslashes that precedes a closing (or embedded) quote in `quote_windows`, or have the elevator refuse an argument ending in a backslash that needs quoting; add a case to the Windows elevator guard test or a pure `command_line` rendering test.

**Expected:** `.github/workflows/pr-test.yml` installs `nightly-2026-06-23` (with `rust-src` and wasm32) in every job whose steps now run `cargo +nightly-2026-06-23`. **Observed:** the install step was added only to the `wasm-playwright` job (line ~124). The `rust-validation` job (name "Rust Workspace") still sets up only stable and then runs `cargo run -p xtask -- app apps/lab build wasm` and `app apps/test_suite build wasm ...` (lines ~87-90). Those now invoke `cargo +nightly-2026-06-23 build -Z build-std`, and a dated toolchain cannot be a runner-preinstalled `nightly`, so the job fails with 'toolchain is not installed'. **Repair:** add the same 'Setup the threaded-WASM nightly' step (`dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master`, `toolchain: nightly-2026-06-23`, `components: rust-src`, `targets: wasm32-unknown-unknown`) to `rust-validation` after 'Setup Rust' (or rustup-install it via `rustup toolchain install nightly-2026-06-23 --profile minimal --component rust-src --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`), and update the reference table in `wasm-toolchain-update.md` accordingly.

**Expected:** the reference's closing verification (`wasm-toolchain-update.md` lines ~52-56) is a `git grep` that finds nothing once the pin is consistent. **Observed:** it says `git grep -n nightly -- . ':(exclude).agentx' ':(exclude)vendor' | grep -v 'nightly-[0-9]'` 'finds nothing' in RayX and Gpux, but that command matches prose such as 'nightly `-Z build-std`', 'nightly schedule' and 'nightly pipeline' (about 14 lines in RayX and 24 in Gpux outside `crates/`), so an agent following it will conclude the move is incomplete or chase false hits. **Repair:** replace it with the sprint's own pattern: `git grep -n -P '\+nightly(?!-\d)|toolchain install nightly(?!-\d)|--toolchain nightly(?!-\d)|"nightly"' -- . ':(exclude).agentx' ':(exclude)vendor' ':(exclude)crates'` (Gpux) and the same without the `crates` and `vendor` excludes (RayX), which find nothing when the pins are consistent; state that Gpux's `crates/` is excluded because of the `nightly` cargo feature and the `hello_web` example toolchain file.

**Expected:** doc comments agree with the new default. **Observed:** `gpux:tooling/testkit/src/web.rs:25` still says `TOOLCHAIN_ENV_VAR` overrides the nightly toolchain '(`nightly` by default)', directly above the new `DEFAULT_TOOLCHAIN = "nightly-2026-06-23"`. **Repair:** change it to 'overrides [`DEFAULT_TOOLCHAIN`]'.
Resolved: both discovery cargo calls (and the Windows `rustup show` probe) set `RUSTUP_AUTO_INSTALL=0`; `discovery_asks_rustup_not_to_install_anything` asserts it.

Resolved: discovery falls back to `Project::discover_from_files` (nearest enclosing workspace, members, package and workspace `metadata.rayx`); pins then resolve from files. Covered by the missing-toolchain fixture, the scripted-cargo-failure tests on pinned-app and gpux-checkout, and the no-manifest negative test.

Resolved: on Windows the toolchain probe requires the native triple suffix, an unpinned run requires a `(default)` entry, and the unpinned install is `rustup toolchain install stable` then `rustup default stable`.
Resolved: `probe_packages` requires the second `Status-Abbrev` character `i`.
Resolved: `Cx::with_clt_marker` injects a real marker path; tests assert the marker exists at `softwareupdate --list` and `--install` time and is removed after success and after a failed install.
Resolved: apostrophes in the rustup-init path are doubled for PowerShell.
Resolved: with `--yes` the Homebrew step runs an interactive `sudo -v` before the NONINTERACTIVE installer; no sudo without `--yes`.

**Delta verified:** `find_tool`/`which_all`/`node_command` now find node, corepack and pnpm in PATH (skipping /mnt under WSL) and the known install locations, and run them by absolute path. The node step and the corepack call are fixed.

**Still open (Windows first run, and macOS with keg-only node):** `src/setup/test_tools.rs:85-88` (`node_command`), `:187-197` (pnpm probe), `:205-217`, `:233-238`, `:333-340`. The pnpm that `corepack enable --install-directory <user bin>` writes is a shim that starts `node` *by name from PATH* when no `node.exe` sits beside it. I generated one on this host: `pnpm.CMD` contains `@IF EXIST "%~dp0\node.exe" (...) ELSE (... node "...corepack\dist\pnpm.js" %*)`. Run with a PATH that lacks Node (`PATH=C:\Windows\System32`) it prints `'node' is not recognized` and exits 1. On a fresh Windows machine `winget install OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS` does not change this process's PATH, so `pnpm --version` (the pnpm probe and its re-probe) fails with "pnpm does not run" and the step fails after install; the later `pnpm install` / `pnpm exec playwright install` would fail the same way. On macOS the shim is `#!/usr/bin/env node`, which fails the same way while the keg-only `node@<major>/bin` is not on PATH. The new tests cannot show this: the fixtures only prove that the absolute path is chosen.

**Repair:** for every spec that runs pnpm, corepack or node (`node_command`, the node/pnpm `--version` queries), set `PATH` in the spec env to the directory of the found `node` (and the user bin dir) prepended to the machine's PATH; this is the one place the process PATH needs correcting. Add a test asserting the pnpm commands carry that PATH entry when node was found only in a known location (Windows `%ProgramFiles%\nodejs`, Homebrew keg).

**Where:** `src/setup/ios.rs:27-37` (`xcode_version`), step order `:313-321`, selection `:14-24` and `:126-130`.

**Expected:** the Xcode step is satisfied by an installed Xcode at the pinned version and is met right after `xcodes`/`mas` installed it; `xcode-select --switch` then points at the pinned Xcode.

**Observed:**
1. The Xcode probe runs `xcodebuild -version`. That fails (exit 1/69) whenever the active developer directory is the Command Line Tools or the license is not accepted. Right after `xcodes install` the CLT are still selected and the license is pending (the select and license steps come after the xcode step), so the re-probe fails and `rayx setup --ios` stops with "Xcode ... is still missing after its install ran" on the first run of every fresh Mac. An Xcode.app that is installed but unselected, or whose license changed after an update, is likewise reported missing and its multi-GB download is started again. The test fixture `bare()` (CLT selected, `xcodebuild` exits 1) encodes this state as "Xcode missing".
2. `xcode_apps(..).pop()` takes the lexicographically last `Xcode*.app` and ignores the pin. With `Xcode-16.2.0.app` and `Xcode.app` or `Xcode-26.1.0.app` installed and a pin of 16.2, it switches to the other app, the probe then sees the wrong version, `xcodes install 16.2` is a no-op, and the step can never be satisfied. `Xcode-16.10` also sorts before `Xcode-16.2`.

**Repair:** read the installed version without depending on selection or license, for example from `/Applications/Xcode*.app/Contents/version.plist` (`CFBundleShortVersionString`), and treat the step as satisfied when an app matching the pin (or any app when unpinned) exists. Make `xcode-select --switch` choose the app that matches the pin (else the highest by numeric version, not by name). Add tests: Xcode.app present with CLT selected and license pending (no download, only select/license), and a pinned version with a newer Xcode also installed.

**Where:** `src/setup/android.rs:595-598` (AVD probe).

**Expected:** the default AVD is created when no AVD exists, as RayX xtask's `first_android_avd_name` decides (it skips `INFO |`, `WARNING |`, `ERROR |`, `DEBUG |` log lines that `emulator -list-avds` can print on stdout, for example the crashdata notice).

**Observed:** the probe treats any non-blank stdout line as an AVD. Emulator builds that print `INFO    | Storing crashdata in: ...` make the step "present" on a machine with no AVD, so `rayx app ... run android` has nothing to start and `setup`/`doctor` report success. The port dropped the xtask filter; the test only feeds a bare AVD name.

**Repair:** reuse xtask's filter (ignore lines whose prefix before `|` is INFO/WARNING/ERROR/DEBUG) and add a test with a log line plus no AVD (missing) and a log line plus an AVD (present).

**Where:** `src/project/pins.rs:175` (system image pin independent of the platform pin), used at `src/setup/android.rs:497` and `:614-618`, AVD name at `:565-571`.

**Expected:** SETUP-7: "a system image for the host CPU (`x86_64` or `arm64-v8a`) at the pinned platform", and the default AVD `rayx-<platform>-<abi>` uses it.

**Observed:** `android-system-image` defaults to `android-34;google_apis` whatever `android-platform` is. In a gpux checkout (profile `android-36`) or a project with `android-platform = "android-35"`, the plan installs `platforms;android-36` but the image `system-images;android-34;google_apis;<abi>`, and creates an AVD named `rayx-android-36-<abi>` backed by an android-34 image. No test pins a platform and checks the image.

**Repair:** when `android-system-image` is not set explicitly, derive it from the resolved platform pin (`<platform>;google_apis`, reporting the platform pin's source), keep the explicit key as an override, and add tests for the gpux profile and for a project platform pin (package list and AVD name/image).

**Where:** `src/setup/android.rs:39-45` (`cmdline_tool`), pinned by `tests/setup_android.rs` `windows_runs_the_batch_tools_through_cmd`.

**Expected:** `sdkmanager.bat` and `avdmanager.bat` start correctly for any SDK location, including `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Android\Sdk` under a user name with a space.

**Observed:** the tool is started as `cmd /c <path> --sdk_root=<sdk> ...`. With a space in the SDK path both the program path and `--sdk_root=...` are quoted, and `cmd /c` then sees a line that starts with a quote and holds more than two, strips the first and last quote and fails (`'C:\Users\First' is not recognized`). Rust already launches a `.bat` given by full path safely, which is what RayX xtask does.

**Repair:** run the `.bat` path directly (`CommandSpec::new(path)`), drop the `cmd /c` wrapper for these two tools, and change the test to assert that a path with a space is passed as the program. (`node_tool` is not affected: its first token after `/c` is not a quote.) Also resolve `avdmanager` with `find_sdkmanager`'s layout search instead of the fixed `cmdline-tools/latest` at `:609-613`.

**Where:** probes across `src/setup/*.rs` (only `web.rs:115-120`, `test_tools.rs:70-72` and `ios.rs:59-65` call `with_found`); `src/doctor.rs:367-373`.

**Expected:** DOCTOR-1: each requirement is reported present with its version, missing, or wrong version.

**Observed:** only wasm-bindgen, Node (major) and Xcode record a version. The JDK, Rust toolchains, nightly, pnpm, Android NDK/platform/build-tools, cargo-ndk and the rest are "present" with no version, and an installed-but-wrong JDK (for example 17), NDK or toolchain is reported as `missing`, never `wrong-version`.

**Repair:** record `found` in the probes that already read a version (pnpm `--version`, `jdk_major_at`, the installed NDK directory, the rustup toolchain name, cargo-ndk version) and set it for the wrong-version cases (a JDK of another major, an NDK of another revision) so doctor can say `wrong-version`; extend `requirements_are_present_missing_or_at_the_wrong_version_with_their_fix` accordingly.

**Where:** `src/doctor.rs:396-397`, `src/setup/gpu.rs:99-101` and `:241` (`parse_lspci` builds `software: false` adapters).

**Expected:** DOCTOR-1: `hardwareAdapter` says whether a hardware adapter is usable.

**Observed:** `hardwareAdapter` is `any(!software)`. On Linux every `lspci` display controller counts as hardware, so an NVIDIA card with no driver (the very case the gpu step reports as missing) or a VM's virtio/VMware display (llvmpipe only) gives `hardwareAdapter: true`. Under WSL the Windows host's adapters count, yet the doctor text "no hardware adapter is visible from WSL" is derived from that value, not from `/dev/dxg` or a non-CPU Vulkan device.

**Repair:** on Linux mark an lspci adapter usable only when a non-CPU Vulkan device with the same vendor id exists (the `has_driver` rule); under WSL require `/dev/dxg` (or a non-CPU `vulkaninfo` device); compute `hardwareAdapter` from that and add fixtures (NVIDIA without driver, VM display, WSL without `/dev/dxg`).

**Where:** `src/setup/test_tools.rs:236-241` (probe ignores `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=0`) versus `:333-343` (install inherits the environment).

**Expected:** SETUP-6 and the RayX rule: use Playwright's per-user browser cache, never `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=0`.

**Observed:** with `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=0` in the user's environment the probe looks in the per-user cache, but `pnpm exec playwright install chromium` installs into `node_modules/.local-browsers`, so the step is never satisfied and setup fails after install on every run.

**Repair:** pass `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=<browser_cache path>` explicitly on the install command, so the cache the probe checks is the cache the install writes; add a test with the variable set to `0`.

**Where:** `src/setup/gpu.rs:541-548` (`vulkan_tools_step`), `:383-398` (`has_driver`), `:452-490` (install actions).

**Expected:** Linux detection with `lspci` plus `vulkaninfo --summary`, and a step that can be met or reports what to do.

**Observed:** (1) nothing installs `pciutils`, so on a minimal Ubuntu `lspci` is missing, no adapters are found and the step reports satisfied ("no GPU adapters were found"). (2) An adapter with an unknown vendor (virtio, VMware, Hyper-V, QEMU) never has a non-CPU Vulkan device, so the step stays missing forever; its install actions are empty and the final notice wrongly says "Restart for the NVIDIA driver".

**Repair:** add `pciutils` to the apt packages of the vulkan-tools step; treat `Vendor::Other` and virtual display adapters as informational (not a missing driver) and make the no-action case report "nothing to install" rather than the NVIDIA restart notice.

**Where:** `src/setup/test_tools.rs:269-279` (`playwright-packages` probe).

**Expected:** like RayX `setup-wasm` (which ran `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline` every time), a changed `pnpm-lock.yaml` leads to a refreshed `node_modules`.

**Observed:** the step is satisfied whenever `node_modules` exists, so a lockfile or Playwright version change after the first install is never applied by `rayx setup --test`; the Chromium probe then reads the stale `playwright-core/browsers.json`.

**Repair:** compare `pnpm-lock.yaml` with `node_modules/.pnpm/lock.yaml` (or `.modules.yaml`) in the probe, or always run the idempotent install when `package.json` exists.

**Expected:** `rayx app <dir> test android|ios|mobile` fails with the clear "not supported yet" message (APP-6), and an unsupported action/target pair such as `deploy wasm` fails with its own message, on any machine, before anything is probed or installed (APP-7: prerequisites are for commands that will build).

**Observed:** `app_command` in `src/app/mod.rs` calls `prereqs::ensure_for_command` before dispatching to `test_target` / `deploy_target`, and `prereqs::required_sets` maps `("test", "android")` to the Android set and `("test", "ios")` to the iOS set (and `("deploy", "wasm")` to the web set). On a machine without the Android SDK or Xcode, `rayx app x test android` therefore offers to install the Android set, or stops with `missing: ... run rayx setup --android`, instead of saying the target is unsupported. The tests for the message (`android_and_ios_tests_say_they_are_not_supported_yet`) use `run_unchecked`, which skips the prerequisite step, so they cannot see this. Found by reading the code; it does not reproduce on this fully provisioned machine.

**Repair:** reject action/target pairs that cannot run (`test` on android/ios/mobile, `deploy` on anything but android, unknown targets) before `prereqs::ensure_for_command`, or make `required_sets` return no sets for them. Add an assertion to `tests/app_prereqs.rs` (for example `required_sets("test", "android")` and `required_sets("deploy", "wasm")` are empty) so the check covers the checked path.

**Resolved:** `check_supported` in `src/app/mod.rs` runs before `prereqs::ensure_for_command` and returns the same messages the dispatch functions give (unknown build/run/pack/publish target, deploy only for android, test not supported for android/ios/mobile, unknown test target, unknown action); `assets` returns earlier and is unaffected. The dispatch functions are unchanged. `tests/app_prereqs.rs::unsupported_action_target_pairs_fail_before_anything_is_offered_for_install` covers it (app_prereqs: 13 passed).

**Expected (WSL-4, d-wsl):** the one elevated child compacts the registry-reported `ext4.vhdx` for any valid install location, and nothing the user-writable registry or a profile path contains can change what the elevated script does. **Observed:** `compact_script` (`src/wsl.rs`) embeds the path in a PowerShell single-quoted literal and only doubles the ASCII `'`. PowerShell also ends a single-quoted string at U+2018, U+2019, U+201A and U+201B (reproduced with `powershell -EncodedCommand`: a path with one `’` gives `TerminatorExpectedAtEndOfString`, exit 1). Consequences: (1) a profile or `BasePath` containing such a character makes the compaction fail only after `wsl --shutdown` has already stopped every distribution and Docker; (2) `BasePath` is read from `HKCU`, which any unelevated process can write, and the script is passed to the elevated child as base64 `-EncodedCommand`, so the runner's quote/`%`/newline guard never sees it: a value like `x’; <command>; ’` runs elevated behind a UAC prompt that only says PowerShell. `tests/wsl_disk.rs` only tests the ASCII quote. **Repair:** do not interpolate the path as code. Pass it as data (for example a second base64 or hex segment decoded inside the script, or an environment variable set on the elevated spec) or at least reject any path containing a control character or any of `'‘’‚‛"` before building the script, and double all four Unicode quotes. Validate before `wsl --shutdown` that the path ends in `.vhdx` and exists (`before.is_some()`), so a bad path stops before anything is shut down. Add a `tests/wsl_disk.rs` case for a path with `’` and with `'; calc; '`.
